events.title: St. Gregory the Great is consecrated Pope
events.shortBlurb: The reluctant monk was consecrated Bishop of Rome and began a pontificate that would reshape the medieval Church…
body: The year 589 closed in disaster for Rome: the Tiber burst its banks, sweeping away houses and the granaries of the Church, and pestilence followed on the flood. In February 590 Pope Pelagius II died of the plague, and the clergy and people with one mind chose Gregory, abbot of St. Andrew's, to succeed him.

Gregory shrank from the office. He wrote to the Emperor Maurice begging him not to confirm the election, but the prefect Germanus suppressed the letter; and tradition adds that he fled the city in a merchant's basket and lay hidden until he was found. While awaiting the emperor's answer he ordered a sevenfold litany, seven companies processing from seven churches to St. Mary Major to beg the plague's end.

Legend holds that as the procession passed the mausoleum of Hadrian he saw the archangel Michael sheathe his sword above it, whence its name Castel Sant'Angelo. The imperial assent came at last, and on 3 September 590 the reluctant monk, the first to take the papal throne, was consecrated; on that day, since his death date falls in Lent, his feast is kept.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), "Pope St. Gregory I (the Great)"
